newsitem.title: USA: Argosy falls after chief executive exits.
newsitem.headline: Argosy falls after chief executive exits.

text.p: Argosy Gaming Inc shares dropped eight percent on Tuesday after the resignation of its chief executive officer and amid analysts' expectations of lower-than-expected casino revenues this winter.
Argosy shares closed down 1/4 Tuesday at 4-1/8, a 52-week low.
"It's a combination of things," said Philip Platek, an analyst at Forum Capital Markets.

He said the stock decline and Long's resignation were obviously connected. "But also their riverboat in Lawrenceburg, Indiana, has posted big numbers on the weekends, but not that much on weekdays," the analyst said.
"The numbers have been lower than expected," Platek said, "but it is January."
Platek added that Argosy's Riverside, Missouri, casino, which serves the Kansas City market, is facing more competition in what's considered a soft market.
"Their numbers are expected to be off," he said.

Argosy earlier said J. Thomas Long resigned as vice chairman, chief executive and as a director to "pursue opportunities in the commercial banking area." Long is expected to remain with Argosy as a consultant through 1999.
"The stock has been weak for quite some time now," said Joseph Coccimiglio, an analyst at Prudential Securities Research.
"There are two problems here -- increased competition, plus the fact there are fewer growth opportunities."
"There haven't been that many opportunities to open more riverboat casinos," Coccimiglio explained, "since states haven't approved more boats."
Company officials were unavailable to comment on the stock activity on Tuesday afternoon.
